item.title: Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
423
ABNT20 KNHC 311143
TWOAT

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
800 AM EDT Mon Aug 31 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Northern Gulf of America (AL97):
An area of low pressure located a little more than 100 miles south
of the coast of southern Louisiana continues to produce a small but
concentrated area of showers and thunderstorms with some signs of
organization. Additional development is expected as the low moves
slowly west-northwestward, and a short-lived tropical depression or
tropical storm is likely to form before the system reaches the Upper
Texas or southwestern Louisiana coasts on Tuesday.

Interests along the southwestern Louisiana and Upper Texas coasts
should monitor the progress of this system, as tropical storm
watches or warnings could be required for portions of the area later
today. Regardless of development, this system is expected to bring
locally heavy rainfall to portions of the Upper Texas and
southwestern Louisiana coasts during the next couple of days. An Air
Force Reserve reconnaissance aircraft is scheduled to investigate
the system this morning. Additional information on this system,
including gale warnings, can be found in High Seas Forecasts issued
by the National Weather Service.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...70 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...70 percent.

Near Hispaniola (Remnants of Dolly):
A surface trough of low pressure (the remnants of Tropical Storm
Dolly) is producing a disorganized area of showers and thunderstorms
that extends from near Hispaniola eastward to the northern Leeward
Islands. Redevelopment, if any, would be slow to occur during the
next few days as the system encounters generally unfavorable
upper-level winds while moving quickly west-northwestward at 20 to
25 mph. Regardless, the system could bring locally heavy rains and
gusty winds to portions of the Leeward Islands, the Virgin Islands,
Puerto Rico, Hispaniola, and the Bahamas during the next couple of
days.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...10 percent.

&&
High Seas Forecasts issued by the National Weather Service can be
found under AWIPS header NFDHSFAT1, WMO header FZNT01 KWBC, and
online at ocean.weather.gov/shtml/NFDHSFAT1.php

$$
Forecaster Reinhart

item.title: Potential Tropical Cyclone Five Public Advisory Number 1
item.description:
Issued at 1000 AM CDT Mon Aug 31 2026 
000
WTNT35 KNHC 311455
TCPAT5
 
BULLETIN
Potential Tropical Cyclone Five Advisory Number   1
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL052026
1000 AM CDT Mon Aug 31 2026
 
...TROPICAL STORM WARNING ISSUED FOR PORTIONS OF THE UPPER TEXAS AND
SOUTHWESTERN LOUISIANA COAST...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1000 AM CDT...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...27.8N 91.0W
ABOUT 130 MI...210 KM S OF MORGAN CITY LOUISIANA
ABOUT 230 MI...365 KM SE OF PORT ARTHUR TEXAS
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...35 MPH...55 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 285 DEGREES AT 5 MPH...7 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1013 MB...29.92 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
A Tropical Storm Warning has been issued for the northwestern Gulf
Coast from Port Bolivar, Texas, to the Vermilion/Cameron Parish
Line in Louisiana.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for...
* Port Bolivar to the Vermilion/Cameron Parish Line
 
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected somewhere within the warning area, in this case within the
next 24-36 hours.
 
For storm information specific to your area, including possible
inland watches and warnings, please monitor products issued by your
local National Weather Service forecast office.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1000 AM CDT (1500 UTC), the disturbance was centered near 
latitude 27.8 North, longitude 91.0 West. The system is moving 
toward the west-northwest near 5 mph (7 km/h), and this general 
motion is expected to continue for the next day or two. On the 
forecast track, the center of the system is predicted reach the 
northwestern Gulf Coast within the warning area on Tuesday.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 35 mph (55 km/h) with higher gusts.
Some strengthening is expected during the next day or so, and the
system is forecast to become a tropical storm by tonight.

* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...80 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...80 percent.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1013 mb (29.92 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Potential Tropical Cyclone Five can be found in the
Tropical Cyclone Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDAT5 and WMO
header WTNT45 KNHC.
 
WIND: Tropical storm conditions are expected to reach the coast
within the warning area on Tuesday, making outside preparations
difficult or dangerous.
 
STORM SURGE: The combination of storm surge and tide will cause
normally dry areas near the coast to be flooded by rising waters
moving inland from the shoreline. The water could reach the
following heights above ground somewhere in the indicated areas if
the peak surge occurs at the time of high tide...
 
High Island, TX to Vermilion/Iberia Parish Line, LA...1-3 ft
 
The deepest water will occur along the immediate coast near and to
the east of the center. Surge-related flooding depends on the
relative timing of the surge and the tidal cycle, and can vary
greatly over short distances. For information specific to your
area, please see products issued by your local National Weather
Service forecast office.
 
For a complete depiction of areas at risk of storm surge
inundation, please see the National Weather Service Peak
Storm Surge Graphic, available at
hurricanes.gov/graphics_at5.shtml?peakSurge.
 
RAINFALL: PTC Five is expected to produce rainfall totals of 3 to 6
inches with maximum totals of 9 inches for parts of the Upper Texas
Coast inland through east-central Texas, with 2 to 3 inches for
Southwest Louisiana. This rainfall could produce flash flooding,
especially in low-lying and urban areas.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next intermediate advisory at 100 PM CDT.
Next complete advisory at 400 PM CDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Reinhart

item.title: Potential Tropical Cyclone Five Forecast Discussion Number 1
item.description:
Issued at 1000 AM CDT Mon Aug 31 2026 
000
WTNT45 KNHC 311456
TCDAT5
 
Potential Tropical Cyclone Five Discussion Number   1
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL052026
1000 AM CDT Mon Aug 31 2026
 
The disturbance (AL97) that the NHC has been tracking over the
northern Gulf of America continues to produce a small area of
showers and thunderstorms with modest signs of organization.
Overnight scatterometer data indicated the circulation lacked
definition on the western side, and recent surface observations and
data from the Air Force Hurricane Hunters suggest the center is
still elongated and ill defined. However, given the expectation that
the system will become a tropical cyclone, and the risk of tropical
storm conditions for portions of the northwestern Gulf Coast, we
are initiating advisories on Potential Tropical Cyclone Five. The
initial intensity is set at a possibly generous 30 kt based on the
overnight scatterometer data.
 
The initial motion is uncertain given the system is still in its 
formative stage, but our best estimate is west-northwestward (285/4 
kt). The track models agree that the system should continue 
west-northwestward during the next day or so and approach the Upper 
Texas and southwestern Louisiana coast within the warning area on 
Tuesday. The official NHC track forecast lies very near the HFIP 
corrected consensus (HCCA), near the center of the guidance 
envelope. A 48-h post-tropical forecast point is shown for 
continuity, but the system will likely be dissipated by that time.
 
The small system is located over SSTs greater than 30 deg C, and the 
deep-layer shear appears fairly weak as diagnosed from the SHIPS 
guidance. Some strengthening is expected before the system reaches 
the coast on Tuesday, as long as it is able to develop a more 
cohesive tropical cyclone structure. Since the center is predicted 
to move onshore between 24-36 h, additional strengthening could 
occur between those forecast points that cannot be reflected in the 
official forecast. Given the anticipated small size of the system, 
it could be prone to quicker intensity changes, so additional 
strengthening beyond what is shown cannot be ruled out. The NHC 
intensity forecast lies at the top of the latest guidance.
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Potential Tropical Cyclone Five is expected to bring tropical
storm conditions to portions of the Upper Texas and southwestern
Louisiana coasts on Tuesday. A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect
from Port Bolivar, Texas, to the Vermilion/Cameron Parish Line,
Louisiana.
 
2. Heavy rain will impact parts of the Upper Texas coast through
east-central Texas into far southwestern Louisiana Tuesday and
Wednesday as the system tracks inland. Flash flooding is likely
across this region, especially in urban areas.
 
3. Minor to moderate coastal flooding is possible along the Upper
Texas and southwestern Louisiana coasts.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  31/1500Z 27.8N  91.0W   30 KT  35 MPH...POTENTIAL TROP CYCLONE
 12H  01/0000Z 28.3N  91.8W   35 KT  40 MPH...TROPICAL CYCLONE
 24H  01/1200Z 29.1N  93.2W   40 KT  45 MPH
 36H  02/0000Z 29.9N  94.4W   35 KT  40 MPH...INLAND
 48H  02/1200Z 31.1N  95.5W   25 KT  30 MPH...POST-TROP/INLAND
 60H  03/0000Z...DISSIPATED
 
$$
Forecaster Reinhart
